transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been having these times after late shifts where I stop for food, and then I get home and keep eating. Like takeout, chips, sweets—whatever’s there. Afterward I kind of look at it and think, “How did I eat that much?”
When you’re eating all that food after getting home, do you feel like you can’t stop or control how much you’re eating?
Yeah… on those nights, once I start, it doesn’t really feel like I’m choosing anymore. I’ll be thinking I should put it away, but I just keep opening things until it’s gone.
Does this eating behavior bother you or cause problems in your daily life, like feeling ashamed or affecting your work or relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I still get to work and all that. But I’ve started avoiding going out to eat with people after shifts. And the next morning I’m usually kind of… trying to make up for the night before instead of just sleeping in or getting things done.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you ever try to compensate by doing something like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Yeah… sometimes. I don’t really like saying it, but after I get home and eat too much, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up. It feels like… so it won’t just sit in me and turn into weight.

latest_inference.note: This turn confirmed compensatory behaviors (e.g., self-induced vomiting) following binge eating episodes, which aligns with the diagnostic criteria for bulimia nervosa (F50.2).
